repository.name: launchbadge/realworld-axum-sqlx
repository.workload: Not supplied — a public RealWorld reference implementation with no stated production traffic.

annotation.notes: Retro-annotated from docs/evaluation.md §3.14, an independent blind pass with no memory of this project's own findings — the second of three untested deep-tier runtime references (JVM, Rust, .NET) closed by this round. Two real correctness bugs (an uncorrelated EXISTS subquery for `favorited`, a feed endpoint missing ORDER BY) were also found and filed under Kind: Correctness, out of the performance rubric entirely per SKILL.md Hard Rule 8 — they are not encoded here, since this schema's category enum matches the performance-finding categories in finding.schema.json and has no correctness axis. `forbidden` is intentionally empty: the pass correctly declined to flag spawn_blocking-offloaded Argon2 hashing as a blocking-call defect (it is the right pattern, confirmed by technology/rust.md's runtime-identification guidance), but no exact file:line for that call site is given in §3.14's "in brief" summary, and inventing one here would violate the same no-invented-facts discipline this corpus exists to hold reviews to.

expected.mechanism: An unauthenticated, unbounded GET /api/tags endpoint runs a full-table DISTINCT-over-unnest scan with no cache and no rate limit. The codebase's own source comment states this query requires a full table scan and is a likely point for a DoS attack — corroborating evidence for the finding, not a claim invented by the review.
limit.unwrap_or(20) is used directly as the SQL LIMIT on two list endpoints with no upper clamp on the caller-supplied value, each returned row carrying two to three correlated subqueries.
No server-side request timeout or body-size limit configured anywhere in the Axum middleware stack — tower-http is included with only its trace feature, not limit or timeout.
The primary unfiltered article-listing sort (ORDER BY created_at) has no supporting index; the schema's only secondary index is the GIN index on tag_list.

Argon2 password hashing is correctly offloaded via spawn_blocking (the right pattern for CPU-bound work in an async handler, not itself a defect), but nothing bounds how many concurrent offloaded hashes can run beyond Tokio's own default blocking-thread-pool cap.
forbidden_recommendation: flag the spawn_blocking offload itself as blocking
